title: Response-weighted Token Importance Sampling for Per-Domain Calibration Micro-Packs
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Design and implement a production-ready sampling strategy that prioritizes prompts for calibration packs based on token-level importance derived from model responses and quantization sensitivity. Deliver compact per-domain 'micro-packs' (approx. 200-400 examples) that maximize accuracy signal for FP8/INT8 profile validation without reprocessing full traffic logs.
background: Existing calibration sampling approaches focus on domain stratification, reservoir sampling, and recency weighting. However, we observe many sampled prompts are low-signal for quantization-induced degradation (e.g., short prompts, generic system messages). We need a finer-grained importance heuristic that combines response sensitivity and token saliency to concentrate calibration effort where quantization changes outputs most.
proposed_approach: Compute a token-level importance score for production request-response pairs by combining: (1) response divergence under candidate quantization profiles (delta-bertscore / token probability shift), (2) token saliency via gradient/attention rollouts on the reference model, and (3) traffic weight (tenant/route frequency). Aggregate scores into per-domain ranked buckets. Build micro-packs by sampling top-ranked exemplar prompts while preserving a small tail of low-frequency and long-context examples for coverage.
sampling_specification:
- Input: anonymized request + canonical response (post-processed)
- Scoring: importance = alpha*prob_shift + beta*saliency + gamma*traffic_weight (alpha=0.6,beta=0.3,gamma=0.1 start)
- Buckets: short (<=64 tok), mid (65-256), long (257-1024)
- Pack target: 250 examples per domain (configurable 200-400)
- Dedup: exact-text and lexical fingerprint dedupe threshold 0.85
- Prefix preservation: retain original prompt prefix up to 2 turns for chat-like domains
- Privacy: strip PII heuristics and replace with domain-appropriate placeholders
calibration_pack_format: JSONL with fields: key, domain, prompt_hash, context_length, importance_score, canonical_response, source_route, anonymized=true, candidate_quant_eval (link)
evaluation_plan: 1) Offline: run candidate FP8/INT8 profiles on a held-out 10k production sample to compute delta metrics for top- vs bottom-ranked buckets. 2) Micro-pack validation: for each domain, run micro-pack through full calibration pipeline and compare post-quantization accuracy to baseline using the same eval harness. 3) Continuous monitoring: surface regression rate per micro-pack on runtime-1.20 and schedule re-sampling if regression > 1.5x baseline.
metrics:
- Pack size (n)
- Coverage: % of top-k traffic covered by pack
- Delta-BERTScore and token-accuracy drop after quantization
- Calibration efficiency: accuracy improvement per 100 examples
- Regression rate in production after rollout
acceptance_criteria: Prototype scoring pipeline implemented and runs weekly over sampled traffic
Per-domain micro-packs generated (>=5 domains) with size 200-400
Offline validation shows >2x sensitivity (delta metric) in top-ranked bucket vs random sample
Calibration using micro-packs reduces post-quantization regression by >=10% vs no calibration
Artifacts (design doc, JSONL exports, dashboards) linked and reviewed by APPLIED ML and Runtime teams
tasks: Add token-saliency module using attention-rollout approximation
Integrate probability-shift comparator for candidate quant profiles
Micro-pack JSONL writer + storage in s3://redwood-calibration/micropacks/
Validation job in eval-harness and dashboard wiring
